people.name: Jay Kapoor
people.bio: Jay Kapoor is a General Partner at VSC Ventures, the host of CLIMB, and the founder of Dirty Jobs, the physical AI event for hard industries. He interviews the founders and investors building autonomy, robotics, and industrial AI, and he is on stage all day on September 23.

people.name: Vijay Chattha
people.role: Founder and Managing Partner, VSC Ventures
people.bio: Vijay Chattha is the founder and Managing Partner of VSC Ventures and the founder of VSC, the communications firm behind hundreds of technology launches. He co-hosts Dirty Jobs and interviews Navin Chaddha in the closing fireside.

people.name: Peter Ludwig
people.bio: Peter Ludwig co-founded Applied Intuition in 2017 and leads the software that runs on more than fifty hardware platforms, from passenger cars to L4 trucks moving commercial loads in Japan. Before Applied he was an engineer at Google. His July essay for a16z argues that the limiting variable in physical AI is no longer the model but the system that validates and deploys it, and his December testimony to the House Select Committee on the CCP put Chinese connected vehicles on the record as a national security question. This is his first solo stage conversation.

people.name: Jagdeep Singh
people.bio: Jagdeep Singh has taken frontier technology into three industries that hate risk. He co-founded Infinera, sold optical networking to telecom carriers, took it public, and saw Nokia acquire it in a $2.3B deal. He co-founded QuantumScape, sold solid-state batteries to automakers, and took it public. Rhoda, his third, came out of stealth in March with a $450M Series A led by Premji Invest with Khosla, Mayfield, and VSC Ventures. Its robots learn from internet video and pick up a new task from 10 to 20 hours of robot data, and they are already moving from pilots into production inside live factories.

people.name: Navin Chaddha
people.bio: Navin Chaddha runs Mayfield, one of the oldest firms in Silicon Valley, and has backed founders through several platform shifts. His current thesis is that the second infrastructure wave under AI looks like deep tech, advanced engineering, and energy systems: power, cooling, optics, memory, switching. Recent checks include Lumilens, Upscale AI, AI Fabrik, and Hang Ten, three of them to founders he has backed before. He is on record that nobody can see five years out in AI, and he still sizes markets over five to seven year windows. The closing conversation is about what has to be true about a business model before physical AI is investable at Mayfield's scale.

people.name: Michael Brisbois
people.bio: Michael Brisbois leads West Coast sales at Bright Data, the web data platform that supplies training and evaluation data to AI teams, and the title partner of Dirty Jobs 2026. He came to Bright Data from Amazon.

people.name: Julian Nash
people.bio: Julian Nash is a Managing Director at Silicon Valley Bank, a division of First Citizens Bank, where he works with venture-backed technology companies and the funds that back them. SVB is the innovation banking partner of Dirty Jobs 2026.

people.name: Rita Astoor
people.bio: Rita Astoor leads fund partnerships at Carta, the fund administration and equity platform, and lectures at UC Berkeley School of Law. Carta is the fund admin partner of Dirty Jobs 2026.

people.name: Yashreeka Huq
people.bio: Yashreeka Huq is a Partner at Ashurst Perkins Coie, where she advises emerging companies and the investors who fund them. The firm is the legal services partner of Dirty Jobs 2026.

people.name: Saman Farid
people.bio: Saman Farid is the founder and CEO of Formic, which puts robots into American factories on a robots-as-a-service model so manufacturers pay for output instead of capital equipment. He is a past CLIMB guest and a Dirty Jobs 2026 sponsor.

people.name: Eshan Jayamanne
people.bio: Eshan Jayamanne is the founder and CEO of Krane, which builds software for the construction industry. A licensed engineer and Stanford GSB alumnus, he is a Dirty Jobs 2026 sponsor.

people.name: Aaron Campbell
people.bio: Aaron Campbell is the CEO of Operation Autopilot, a Dirty Jobs 2026 sponsor building autonomy for physical operations.

people.name: Tommy Leep
people.bio: Tommy Leep runs venture partnerships at Google Cloud, connecting startups and their investors to Google's infrastructure and AI stack. Google Cloud is a supporting partner of Dirty Jobs 2026 and moderates a session.
